newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Shareholding in BT hedged by put purchase.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Shareholding in BT hedged by put purchase.

text.p: One of the larger deals in UK equity options on Tuesday was in British Telecommunications, in which put options were bought to protect a shareholding in the company, dealers said.
The deal was to buy 1,600 August 420 puts at 12p against buying 1.6 million shares at 458p.
If BT's share price falls sufficiently, then losses from the shareholding will be limited by exercising the puts in order to sell stock at 420p.
On the other hand, if the share price rises, profits from the stockholding will be reduced by the cost of the puts.
By 1405 GMT, BT shares were up 1-1/2p to 458-1/2p.
The swift rise in banking shares prompted some traders to close bearish positions. One such deal was in HSBC Holdings, in which around 750 July 1450 puts were sold at prices between 6p and 7p.
Similarly in Lloyds TSB Group, there was a seller of about 520 June 360 puts at 1/2p and in a separate deal, 460 June 460 puts were sold at 3p.
Shares in HSBC jumped up 16-1/2p to 1700p while those of Lloyds TSB added 13-1/2p to 569-1/2p.

Over in tobacco-to-insurance group B.A.T Industries the main deal was a long straddle in expectation of increased volatility in the stock. The deal involved the purchase of 200 July 550 puts and calls at 36p and 25-1/2p each.
Elsewhere, in FTSE 100 index options the biggest deal was from a buyer of 5,000 June 4650 calls at 27-1/2p expecting the market to continue rising.
At 1355 GMT, the index was up 60.5 points to 4516.1.
